framework: SAMHSA's Eight Dimensions of Wellness (adapted from Swarbrick, 2006)

tiers.name: Stabilizing resources
tiers.line: Plan an accessible solution someone can use for themselves.

dimensions.name: Emotional
dimensions.summary: Wellbeing starts with someone who shows up. Our peers are there every day, as equals.
tiers: Daily connection and a co-equal relationship with peers
Care referrals, and our continued daily presence
Continued support to each individual

dimensions.name: Occupational
dimensions.summary: Work and purpose depend on being able to get there, and to show up as yourself.
tiers: Reliable transportation (bus passes, bike locks) and professional clothing
Referrals for job placement programs, and résumé assistance
Ongoing individualized support

dimensions.name: Intellectual
dimensions.summary: Curiosity doesn't wait for housing. Learning is part of how people rebuild.
tiers: Art, poetry and movie workshops, and supplies
Exploration: referrals and information for classes, groups and events
Program enrollments for education and more, with ongoing goal-setting and support

dimensions.name: Environmental
dimensions.summary: The spaces people live in, and move through, shape everything else.
tiers: Park cleanup, sleeping bags or blankets, clothing
Laundry vouchers, plus referrals and information for shelters and free, friendly public spaces with bathrooms, showers and storage
Housing and furniture

dimensions.name: Financial
dimensions.summary: Money is a barrier at every step. We remove it first, then help people build a way forward.
tiers: Essentials provided at no cost
Enrollment and advocacy for Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), SSI and SSDI
Long-term goal setting and individualized planning

dimensions.name: Social
dimensions.summary: Belonging is basic. It starts with conversation and grows into community.
tiers: Conversation and companionship with peers
Continued daily interaction, deepening connection, and prosocial events
A broadened sense of community

dimensions.name: Physical
dimensions.summary: Food, water, first aid and harm reduction come first, wherever someone is.
tiers: Nutritious food and water, hygiene supplies, basic wound care, safe-use and harm reduction supplies, and safer-sex supplies
Food bank information, care referrals, and SNAP and Medicaid enrollment
Housing and advocacy

dimensions.name: Spiritual
dimensions.summary: Meaning looks different for everyone. We make room for whatever it is for you.
tiers: Outreach by the faith groups that join our events
Conversation, and referrals to programs and groups that fit each person
Ongoing follow-up
